page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Daldv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 1890 GB of local NVMe storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core metrics placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is also robust, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top 25%, while stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores sit in the middle 50%. Memory performance is highly rated, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, despite uncached read and write memory bandwidths remaining in the average tier. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, and strong performance in image processing, text processing, and CPU encryption tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32alds_v6 offers a balanced profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, optimizing resource spend by pairing high-frequency AMD EPYC processing with a lean 2.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage provides high-speed scratch space without the added cost of external block storage. This hardware configuration is well-suited for compute-intensive tasks, software compilation, image processing, cryptography, and lightweight large language model inference.
